item.title: Federal fudges speaking out after unprecedented wave of threats, intimidation and attacks
item.description: Judges are now speaking out when attacked, to combat misinformation, and to preserve the integrity of the judicial system. So far this year, the U.S. Marshals Service has already recorded 241 threats against judges in 2026, after 564 threats in 2025.

item.title: Englewood community resource center broken into, burglarized, organizers say
item.description: For years, a community center on the South Side has been a safe haven for families in an area that often sees crime. Now, the center itself has been targeted.

item.title: Robbery victim shoots, kills armed 16-year-old suspect in West Pullman, Chicago police say
item.description: Chicago police are investigating after a man shot and killed a teenager who was trying to rob him, officials said.

item.title: Chicago City Council votes to freeze wage increases for tipped workers, Mayor Johnson vows to veto
item.description: An ordinance was established two years ago to slowly increase wages for tipped workers. On Wednesday, a majority of city aldermen voted to halt the automatic increases. Mayor Brandon Johnson vowed to veto the freeze.

item.description: Funeral arrangements have been announced for Chicago firefighter Michael Altman.

item.title: Chicago-area native college student James Gracey missing in Spain during spring break trip
item.description: Elmhurst native 20-year-old college student James Gracey has gone missing in Spain, his family said. Local media in Spain is reporting that Gracey was seen leaving a club with another person.
